scope: Corrected Cosmos-Predict2 14B DROID baseline with CPU T5 encoding
summary: The device-correct CPU T5 route loaded the tokenizer and verified 14B DiT on all four ranks, then was deliberately stopped before sampling because each context-parallel rank redundantly encoded both prompts with T5-11B on a single CPU thread under extreme shared-host load.
evidence: All four workers initialized context parallelism and the log records successful tokenizer, T5, and 14B DiT loading.
The corrected helper passed CPU token IDs to CPU T5 weights; the earlier CUDA-versus-CPU embedding error did not recur.
Four workers remained CPU-active after entering the pipeline while GPU utilization stayed at zero and the run log did not reach video sampling.
The process group was terminated deliberately, selected GPU memory returned to its pre-run state, and no generated video exists.
lessons: Context-parallel inference must not instantiate and run the same T5-11B encoder independently on every rank.
Positive and fixed negative prompt embeddings can be computed once on one audited GPU, pinned by SHA-256, and loaded by every rank while constructing the video pipeline with use_text_encoder=false.
limitations: This attempt contains no generated frames and is not video-quality evidence.
next_actions: Precompute the legacy-development prompts and official fixed negative prompt once, add strict embedding-contract validation, and rerun the baseline in a new experiment directory.
